title: Affine algebraic-space maps have no positive quasi-coherent higher direct images
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:Y\to X$ be affine, meaning representable with affine scheme base changes. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ for its underlying additive sheaf. For the induced direct image $f_*:\operatorname{Ab}(Y_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$, let $R^qf_*$ denote its right derived functors, computed by injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then $R^qf_*(F_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every integer $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 073H, lemma-affine-vanishing-higher-direct-images; higher direct images interpreted on underlying additive sheaves as in sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-limp-acyclic and lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree.

proof.text: Fix $q>0$. Since $f$ is representable, $u(V)=W=Y\times_XV$ is a scheme for every scheme object $V\to X$. Etale base-change permanence makes $W\to Y$ an object of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ and makes $u$ continuous. The canonical small-etale morphism of topoi is the one induced by this base-change functor: the enlarged-site model restricts to this functor here because its values on scheme objects are schemes. The site higher-direct-image formula therefore identifies $R^qf_*F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $P^\#$, where $P(V)=H^q(W,F_{\mathrm{ab}})$ is cohomology over the object $W\to Y$.

Now take $V\to X$ with $V$ affine. By the stated meaning of affineness, $W=Y\times_XV$ is an affine scheme. Put $h:W\to Y$. Its etale module pullback is restriction, and pullback preserves quasi-coherence. Thus $F|_W$ is quasi-coherent on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply the quasi-coherent groupoid equivalence to the identity atlas $W\to W$: the relation groupoid is the identity groupoid, so its underlying quasi-coherent scheme module is a module $M$ on $W$ whose associated etale module is $F|_W$. In particular its underlying additive sheaf is $M_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 03M3, proposition-quasi-coherent, including the scheme etale/Zariski convention in its proof; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 073H

proof.text: Postcomposition gives an equivalence $W_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq Y_{\mathrm{et}}/W$: objects in both are scheme maps $T\to W$, and the etale permanence statement says $T\to W$ is etale if and only if $T\to Y$ is etale. The reverse implication applies its assertion that a map between etale objects over $Y$ is etale; the forward implication is composition. Arrows are the same maps over $W$, and coverings are the same jointly surjective etale families. Object-cohomology localization followed by invariance under this site equivalence identifies $H^q(W,F_{\mathrm{ab}})$ with $H^q(W_{\mathrm{et}},(F|_W)_{\mathrm{ab}})$. By step 2 and affine etale quasi-coherent acyclicity, this is $H^q(W_{\mathrm{et}},M_{\mathrm{et}})=0$. Hence $P(V)=0$ on every affine etale test object.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open; descent.tex Tag 03DW, proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent (affine vanishing in its proof)

proof.text: Every scheme object $V\to X$ has an affine open covering $V_i\to V$, which is also an etale covering. If $a:P\to G$ is any map to an abelian sheaf, the image of $s\in P(V)$ restricts to zero on each $V_i$, since $P(V_i)=0$. The separatedness part of the sheaf axiom forces $a_V(s)=0$. Thus the only map $P\to G$ is zero, for every sheaf $G$. By the universal property of sheafification, the identity and zero endomorphisms of $P^\#$ coincide. Therefore $P^\#=0$, and step 1 gives $R^qf_*F_{\mathrm{ab}}=0$. The argument applies to each $q>0$.

lean.note: The higher image is the homology of canonical abelian direct image applied to an arbitrary injective resolution of F_ab. This is the injective-resolution definition of R^q f_* in the node, without changing to module-derived images or adding a resolution-existence assumption. The source and target retain AddCommGrpCat.{u} on the full small etale sites.
